blindSummary: A 2026 law (enacted February 2026 over the governor's veto) confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in government buildings and creates a private right of action letting anyone sue a person they suspect of violating it for roughly one thousand units of the local currency — a bounty-hunter mechanism that exposes visitors directly. It also invalidates identity documents issued by the state/province with corrected gender markers. This is the first state/province in the country flagged in the assessment's harshest tier this cycle; two trans men sued within days citing fear of violence. Local risk sits below the country-wide average.
